# Vendored upstreams

<!-- GENERATED by `pf vendor doc` from platform/src/pf/vendor/registry.yaml.
     Edit the registry, not this file. -->

10 upstreams, pinned as submodules under `vendor/`. 53 adoptions, 22 explicit declines.

Every borrowing below is a path pair — one file upstream, one or more of
ours — so the claim is verifiable rather than remembered. `pf vendor verify`
fails if an upstream path stops existing; `pf vendor drift` names the files
of ours that an upstream change implicates.

## How the pins stay current

```bash
pf vendor list          # every upstream, licence, pinned commit, state
pf vendor sync          # fetch each tracking branch, then report
pf vendor drift         # what moved since a human last looked
pf vendor approve <id>  # record the current checkout as reviewed
pf vendor verify        # declared paths still exist; contracts still hold
pf vendor why <file>    # where did this file of ours come from
```

`.gitmodules` carries `branch =` for each, so `git submodule update --remote`
follows the upstream default branch. The eight added most recently are
`shallow = true` — we want the tip, never the history.

**`vendor.lock.json` is not the gitlink.** The submodule pointer records which
commit is checked out; the lock records which commit a person *reviewed*, plus
a git OID per adopted path. Those diverge the moment someone runs `--remote`
without reading anything, and the gap between them is the only thing that makes
drift observable. An upstream that moved forty commits without touching
anything we adopted is a free fast-forward; one that touched a schema stops.

Automation runs weekly (`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml`) and opens a PR.
It never approves — approval means a human read the diff, and a workflow
cannot mean that.

## Coupling kinds

| kind | meaning | an upstream change… |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | our output is validated against the vendored file | can fail a build |
| `data` | we read the file at runtime | changes behaviour |
| `parity` | we check our structure against upstream's required fields | means we may be missing a concept |
| `port` | we reimplemented it for our runtime | means re-read one of our files |
| `shape` | we adopted a structure or an idea | is informational |

## Licence review outstanding

### `dlthub-ai-workbench` — dltHub License (proprietary)

Scope-of-use is limited to dltHub Services. This platform runs dlt Core on Dagster, which reads as a third-party orchestration service under the "NOT permitted" examples. Our dlt toolkits are independent rewrites against dlt Core's public API for that reason, and the submodule is pinned for reference and drift detection rather than redistribution. Confirm with counsel before shipping this platform externally.

### `evidence-bi` — not stated upstream

No LICENSE file at the upstream root as of the pinned commit. Treated as reference only: our reporting layer is generated from our own semantic layer, and no upstream file is copied into a project.

## OpenTopology (otop-core)

`opentopology` · [https://github.com/opentopology/opentopology](https://github.com/opentopology/opentopology) · `vendor/opentopology` @ `main` · spec · Apache-2.0

otop's contribution is not entity modelling — it is the traceability chain intent -> constraint -> artifact -> evidence. That is what turns "we have a PII rule" into "here is the check, and here is the run that proves it fired".

### Adopted (2)

- **`schemas/otop-core-v0.2.schema.json`** → `platform/src/pf/projections/otop.py`, `platform/src/pf/ontology/policy.yaml`  ·  _schema_
  Our policy layer is emitted as an otop 0.2 manifest and validated against this exact file. If upstream tightens the schema, the export fails here rather than in a consumer.
- **`specs/otop-core-0.2.md`** → `platform/src/pf/ontology/policy.yaml`  ·  _shape_
  Relationship vocabulary taken verbatim: governed_by, implemented_by, verified_by. Renaming them locally would break every otop consumer.

### Deliberately not taken (2)

- **signatures / attestation blocks** — Nothing signs evidence in this platform yet. An unsigned signature block is worse than none — it implies a guarantee that does not exist.
- **otop-core-0.1 schema** — Superseded by 0.2. We track one version so there is one answer to "does this conform".

## WrenAI

`wrenai` · [https://github.com/Canner/WrenAI](https://github.com/Canner/WrenAI) · `vendor/wrenai` @ `main` · spec · Apache-2.0 for core/**, CC-BY-4.0 for docs/**

MDL is the interchange format a BI or text-to-SQL layer can consume without being told our internals. Emitting it keeps the semantic layer portable.

### Adopted (1)

- **`core/wren-mdl/mdl.schema.json`** → `platform/src/pf/projections/mdl.py`  ·  _schema_
  Field names and the cardinality enum come from this file, not from memory. `layoutVersion` is an integer here — we got that wrong once by guessing, which is the reason the schema is vendored.

### Deliberately not taken (1)

- **The Wren engine, UI and AI service** — Room is left, not taken. We emit a conformant manifest; adopting Wren means pointing it at `mdl/mdl.json`, with nothing else to change.

## Loop Engineering

`loop-engineering` · [https://github.com/cobusgreyling/loop-engineering](https://github.com/cobusgreyling/loop-engineering) · `vendor/loop-engineering` @ `main` · shape · MIT

The governance shape for scheduled agent work: durable state, a path gate, a token budget, a circuit breaker and an autonomy ladder. The patterns are software-delivery loops; the subjects here are data-platform ones.

### Adopted (11)

- **`LOOP.md`** → `LOOP.md`  ·  _shape_
- **`STATE.md`** → `STATE.md`  ·  _shape_
  Generated here, never hand-edited — a hand-edited state file stops being evidence.
- **`gate.yaml`** → `gate.yaml`, `gate.capabilities.yaml`, `platform/hooks/pre_tool_use.py`  ·  _shape_
  Upstream's gate is advisory. Ours is a PreToolUse hook, so the denylist is structural rather than a rule an agent has to remember.
- **`loop-budget.md`** → `loop-budget.md`, `platform/src/pf/loops/runner.py`  ·  _shape_
- **`loop-constraints.md`** → `loop-constraints.md`  ·  _shape_
- **`patterns/registry.yaml`** → `platform/src/pf/loops/registry.py`  ·  _shape_
  Same fields — autonomy level, cadence, token budget, human gates.
- **`patterns/registry.schema.json`** → `platform/src/pf/loops/registry.py`  ·  _parity_
  Field parity, not instance validation. Our loops cannot satisfy the schema literally: `cadence` is a time grammar (`^[0-9]+[mhd]...`) and four of ours are event-driven (pre-commit, on manifest change, on dbt failure), while `file` requires a per-pattern markdown page where ours are one LOOP.md. So `pf vendor verify` asserts the weaker, honest property — every field upstream marks required has a counterpart in LoopSpec. If upstream adds a required governance concept, we are missing it, and that is the signal worth having.
- **`docs/safety.md`** → `platform/src/pf/loops/runner.py`  ·  _shape_
  Circuit breaker — the same failure twice stops the loop rather than retrying it.
- **`skills/loop-verifier/SKILL.md`** → `platform/src/pf/loops/audit.py`  ·  _shape_
- **`patterns/dependency-sweeper.md`** → `platform/src/pf/loops/registry.py`, `platform/src/pf/vendor/model.py`  ·  _shape_
  The direct ancestor of the `vendor-drift` loop: report upstream movement, never apply it. L1 by construction — a submodule bump is a human decision.
- **`patterns/pr-babysitter.md`** → `.github/workflows/pr-report.yml`, `platform/src/pf/pr.py`  ·  _shape_
  Ours reports rather than fixes. The PR comment carries blast radius, vendor drift and readiness; a human still merges.

### Deliberately not taken (2)

- **npx @cobusgreyling/loop-context tooling** — The ledger, budget and circuit breaker are implemented in `pf` so they share the tracking DB with agent spend and impact history. One Node dependency in the critical path of every loop is not worth it.
- **patterns/issue-triage.md, patterns/ci-sweeper.md** — Software-delivery subjects. Our loops watch freshness, drift, metric coverage and PII.
